requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

1. **Use the chapter-derived namespace.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` call the same `chapter_namespace` and `full_requirement_name` helpers for requirements and examples. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` verifies the resulting `requirements.something.foo` name.
2. **Use the same valid-name rules as requirements.** Those roots and `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` use `valid_name`. The same test verifies that an example with `bad name` remains literal.
3. **Include all body Markdown.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` extract the body through `without_options`; `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` renders it. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates]` exercises a single-line body and checks text-change reporting. There is no subject-marked test establishing preservation of a multiline Markdown body.
4. **Exclude surrounding whitespace from the body.** Both collection roots call `.trim()`. None of the supplied subject-marked tests asserts trimming of a nonempty example body. The empty-body test is not a test that a nonempty body's surrounding whitespace is removed while its content remains intact.
5. **Describe a concrete case.**
6. **Include expected behavior in that case.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` rejects empty text but does not establish either semantic property. The successful fixture describes a case and result, but accepting that fixture does not test rejection or assessment of text lacking either property. No implementation or test reachable from the subject's marked roots establishes these obligations.
7. **Contain at least one valid reference to a requirement.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[example_references_requirement]`, called by `collect_definitions`, checks target existence and requirement kind. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_may_reference_their_requirement_with_cite_or_test]` covers valid references, unknown targets, example targets, literal references, and inappropriate roles.
8. **Allow `{cite}` to satisfy that reference obligation.** The same helper and test cover this.
9. **Allow `{test}` to satisfy that reference obligation.** The same helper and test cover this, including examples using only that role.
10. **Make a cited requirement an input to the example's assessment.** The applicable decision exists in `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]`: it reads the subject's references and adds cited definitions to mandatory selectors. This is not reachable from the subject's marked implementation roots and does not mark `requirements.examples.definition`. It needs an `{impl}` reference for this obligation. None of the subject-marked tests asserts that preparing an example assessment includes its cited requirement.
11. **Make a testing example an input to the requirement's assessment.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]` enforces coverage of non-citation incoming references, and `AssessmentSources::prepare` selects incoming test sources. These are not reachable from the subject's marked implementation roots and need subject implementation coverage. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates]` does test the evidence-coverage consequence by removing the requirement's input and asserting the missing `{test}` coverage error.
12. **Keep example directives in fenced code literal.** `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` excludes protected code ranges. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` checks both parsing and rendered literal preservation.

## Additional named boundary coverage

The permitted declaration syntax is implemented by `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` and its `colon_fence` helper: at least three opening colons, immediate directive syntax, and a colon-only closing fence at least as long as the opening fence. The subject-marked tests exercise three-colon examples and an unclosed example, but do not test an example with a longer opening fence, a too-short closing fence, or a longer valid closing fence. The four-colon *requirement* in the rendering test does not exercise those example boundaries. These named fence boundaries need subject-marked tests.

The missing tests above exercise transformations or conditional behavior and qualify for none of the testing exemptions. The assessment-input decisions found outside the marked roots are reference-coverage gaps even though working implementations exist elsewhere. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges these gaps.

text: :::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} requirement_text
The `requirement` string in each evidence file MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.
:::{req} declaration

An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.
